I cannot even begin to tell you how much love I have for this series. I have HUNDREDS of hours logged on KCD/KCD2 and still can't put it down. From blacksmithing and alchemy to fighting in tournaments and wars + everything in between, it has so much to offer each day you wake up in Bohemia. The stories and characters are deeply connected to the lands and it's been so much fun getting to learn about them all.

The game also does an incredible job of recreating real life places. The photos I've seen of Trosky compared to KCD is simply breathtaking. Their attention to detail has truly set the bar for other devs trying to do similar projects. It's not just Trosky either. The entire game is truly a work of art. You'll be up to shenanigans through actual historical castles and towns. I HIIIIIIGHLY recommend this series.

Been a fan of the middle ages since childhood. Wanted something that was not so fantasy oriented like the Witcher or Skyrim, but was more realistic in its depiction of that time period. This fits the bill nicely, beautifully in fact. The scenery, landscape, and its detailing is gorgeous. I could spend hours just walking or riding around and the game lets you spend as much time as you want just soaking it all in. The clothing and armour, the houses, villages and castles appear to be very accurately portrayed ...again you're not in some Hollywood fantasy but have been plunked down some actual 600+ years ago into Bohemian Europe. Being developed by a European studio also adds something I can't quite put my finger on, but it's different from the American studios. One other consideration is that I'm well into my 70s and find many fighting games too fast for my slow reactions, however in this game I'm doing OK so far. In fact I'm totally enjoying it.

Everyone uses the word "masterpiece" loosely; however, this game reminds you every second that it is made by masters of their craft. It embodies in every way the correct philosophy that should lead the future of game design.

Craftsmanship is found in every facet of the game, be it invisible aspects like the optimization of graphical performance, or more striking elements like the research and artisanship that led to such a beautiful world, full of history, and so faithful that every building, every tree, every creek, every person, absolutely everything, looks exactly as you would expect if you went back in time. Even the little details are full of passion and history, like the loading icon or the breathtaking paintings in the loading screen; they look as if painted in another century.

The feeling you get while playing the game is that you truly are in a living, breathing world. Absolutely nothing is bland; everything emanates love and craftsmanship. Additionally, if you take into account all the possible interactions and complex systems used in this game and how well they work, every other game feels so bare bones, bland, and backwards.

This game is so full of things to love, that it is impossible to express in a few words how amazing it really is.

Incredible and memorable game 9/10. It's the medieval brother of Red Dead Redemption 2's western simulator.

The environments, details, and historical accuracy are probably one of the best if not the best in the industry. Forests are absolutely the most immersive in any similar RPG title.

The game has a lot of very unique systems in play that can deter some gamers, but if you are looking for a memorable RPG, be patient and immerse yourself and you'll feel your IRL skills start going up just like Henry. It feels a bit symbiotic.

It is also a dialogue heavy game (with great enough voice acting to actually listen to full conversations). While combat can happen frequently (based on your actions), it's not a combat focused game, but more of a medieval simulator.

and now, ladies and gentlemen, Kingdom Come Deliverance 2.

This is the Line. If you like any of them, the others are a Most to Experience for you.

Overall:
- This is easily one of the best games released this year, so far, if not the best. A true masterpiece of gaming!

What I liked:
- The game is very immersive, engaging and fun. It does make you feel almost like you are the main character, Henry
- The story is interesting, and grabbing. The characters feel well fleshed-out and believable.
- The combat system is interesting, fun, and rewards you mastering it. Swordfighting actually feels like swinging a sword. The choice of weapons is reasonable, and various weapons make sense for different types of situations.
- Crafting is amazing! Whether you're brewing potions, or forging swords, it feel as if you're actually doing it.
- Progression is well thought-out, and you master skills by actually using them. Perks make sense, and actually make you feel like you're becoming better.
- The world is vast, diverse, and full of interesting encounters that develop over time. There are plenty of things to do, and places to explore.
- The world feels historically accurate: the places, the weapons, armour, and where it stops being accurate, it makes complete sense for gameplay reasons. The art style also feels appropriate. Jesus Christ our Lord be praised!
- The performance is very stable and the game looks very good. Watch and learn, Unreal Engine!

What I didn't like:
- The game did crash on me once. And right after I forged like 20 swords. K urw a!

I Finished the game in 180 hours, with all the side quests and published DLCs completed. I had so much fun! The writing is a masterpiece and I really enjoyed the depth of the characters. Occasional crashing happened, but I forgave it as I enjoyed the game otherwise very much. Had to just make sure that I saved often enough, sometimes even by quitting the game and logging back in. The only thing from the immersion side that caught my eye was that there literally are about 5 different faces for NPCs, so having the same face for different characters in side quest caused a bit of confusion. Jesus be praised, this is an amazing game. Huge recommendation and a big thank you for the developers for this masterpiece!

I loved the first game. The second one is worlds better.
Story, gameplay, general decision-making options—it’s all there, and it’s all absolutely brilliant.
The DLCs add a lot to the game. This time, I think the housing system is much better and also fits the story and the character better overall—whereas in the first game it felt like “we just need housing,” here it’s integrated in a way that’s both fitting and beautiful. Still, I wouldn't recommend the Housing DLC until you've finished the main story.
Just like the Story DLC at the monastery, it only makes sense after you've completed the main quest (in both cases, I'm referring strictly to the in-game story logic).
